data.title: Lockheed Martin Stock (LMT) Looks Attractive Despite the Budget Debate
data.description:
Lockheed Martin (LMT) stock looks attractive to me despite uncertainty over next year’s defense budget, because its existing contracts provide strong revenue visibility. The aerospace and defense contractor holds a record $292 billion backlog. CEO Jim Taiclet said the F-35 framework “strengthens the way we can plan and invest in the F-35 enterprise.”

Investors are questioning next year’s Pentagon spending, but production ramps are already underway. I remain bullish on LMT stock because those commitments can support earnings for years, all while shares trade near 17.67x next year’s estimates.

Q3 Shows the Production Ramps Working

Lockheed’s Q3 shows its production ramps working at full speed. Results showed sales rising 11% to $20.7 billion. Earnings per share (EPS) increased 15% to $7.97, and free cash flow (FCF) reached $3 billion. Backlog jumped 27% sequentially to $292 billion. All four segments grew.

Management raised its sales, EPS, and FCF outlook for the second consecutive quarter. I think that broad performance deserves more attention than speculation about one budget.

Missiles and Fire Control led the advance. Sales and operating profit both rose 24% as production of Patriot Advanced Capability-3 (PAC-3) and Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD) increased. Ramps in Guided Multiple Launch Rocket Systems (GMLRS) and Precision Strike Missile (PrSM) also contributed. The missile-segment backlog reached $142.5 billion, up from $46.7 billion at year-end.

The PAC-3 MSE multiyear award totals roughly $58.6 billion, supporting capacity expansion from roughly 600 interceptors annually toward 2,000 by 2030. The seven-year THAAD award is worth up to $35 billion and targets capacity growth from 96 to 400 annually. These ramps still have considerable distance to run.

The opportunity is broadening too. The U.S. Army’s September PrSM Increment 2 award carries a ceiling of $1.2 billion. Extended range (ER) GMLRS received approval to move into production and fielding after successful operational tests.

A recent Navy contract advances PAC-3’s integration with Aegis, opening another potential market. That integration remains under development. However, it illustrates how existing technology can reach additional customers without starting a weapons program from scratch.

The Budget Debate Does Not Erase Demand

The budget debate does not erase demand for Lockheed’s products, in my view. LMT fell 6.9% after Democrats won Congress as investors questioned Trump’s proposed $1.5 trillion 2027 defense budget. Spending could fall materially below that request. Jefferies expects something closer to the House’s $1.15 trillion proposal. Greater scrutiny could delay orders or alter priorities.

Still, a smaller budget increase leaves substantial scope for procurement. Restocking depleted missile inventories remains necessary after years of elevated usage.

The backlog provides a useful perspective. Lockheed expects about 60% to become revenue beyond the next 24 months. That is an unusually long period of visibility. Backlog does not guarantee cash, and future appropriations still matter. Nevertheless, the company is expanding factories against multiyear commitments.

Longer contracts also help suppliers order materials and commit workers earlier. That planning can reduce disruption and improve factory efficiency as output rises. PAC-3 and THAAD capacity is still growing, while PrSM and ER GMLRS are moving into larger-scale production. More output can lift profits even without higher margins.

Allied demand adds another source of orders. These programs span administrations and rely on established manufacturing capabilities that cannot be replaced quickly.

It’s also worth noting that October’s F-35 framework covers 850 U.S. aircraft over 10 years, plus international orders and sustainment. Total production would remain around 156 jets annually. Congressional authorization and appropriations are required before final contracts can be awarded. If completed, the agreement should improve supplier planning and manufacturing efficiency.

There is also an immediate funding issue. Lockheed warned that Lot 20 costs exceeded current authorization and funding. Further delays could pressure cash flow. I take that seriously, but it concerns funding execution for an established platform with decades of expected service ahead.

LMT’s Valuation Looks Reasonable for the Visibility

Lockheed’s valuation looks reasonable considering the visibility discussed above. At today’s price, consensus EPS of $30.69 implies 19.17x 2026 earnings. Forecasts of $33.28 for 2027 and $36.06 for 2028 imply 17.67x and 16.31x. Consensus assumes roughly 8% annual EPS growth in both years. Delivering those estimates would steadily reduce the multiple at today’s price.

That is close to the S&P 500’s (SPX) 17.7x forward multiple. What attracts me is the quality of Lockheed’s prospective earnings. Missile-defense systems and fighter aircraft serve requirements that survive elections. Space systems and nuclear deterrence also require support across successive administrations. High qualification costs and specialized supply chains protect established suppliers.

If production ramps up faster than current assumptions, earnings estimates could rise without investors needing a more generous valuation.

On capital returns, Lockheed raised its quarterly dividend to $3.60, marking 24 consecutive annual increases and yielding about 2.4%. Management expects $7.8–$8 billion of 2026 FCF. Earnings growth alongside that income can support returns with a broadly steady multiple.

Fixed-price charges could absorb some gains, while supplier bottlenecks could delay deliveries. Easing geopolitical tensions might also reduce future orders. I think the existing production commitments provide a substantial cushion, although execution remains essential. In any case, I believe Lockheed Martin’s investment case should remain robust and rather predictable throughout the medium term.

Is Lockheed Martin Stock a Buy?

Lockheed Martin stock has a Moderate Buy consensus, based on nine Buys, eight Holds, and one Sell. The average price target of $649.71 implies 7.72% upside from the stock’s current price levels. If the market begins to recognize that the risks currently facing the company may not be as significant as they seem, I believe the stock could see further upside.

Conclusion

I remain bullish because Lockheed’s investment case extends beyond next year’s budget negotiations. The company is already producing more weapons against years of orders. Political changes can affect funding schedules, but the strategic requirements remain. At 17.67x 2027 earnings, I think investors receive attractive visibility, with upside if expanding production lifts earnings above consensus.

data.title: 3 Real Estate Dividend Stocks Worth Watching
data.description:
VICI Properties (VICI), Realty Income (O), and Agree Realty (ADC) are three real estate dividend stocks worth watching. Real estate stocks can provide dependable dividend income, but dividend quality matters as much as its size. The TipRanks Stock Screener tool helps investors filter stocks by dividend yields and payout ratios.

VICI Properties adds exposure to experiential real estate, including casino and resort properties leased long-term. Realty Income pays its dividend monthly, while Agree Realty combines retail exposure with strong dividend coverage. All three stocks offer dividend yields higher than the real estate sector average yield of 3.135%.

Before we discuss each, a quick note: Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) can have payout ratios that look very high relative to earnings, but depreciation and other non-cash costs drag earnings down. So most investors look at adjusted funds from operations (AFFO), which is closer to the cash a REIT really has to pay dividends.

1. VICI Properties (Yield: 7.30% | Payout Ratio: 83.18%)

VICI Properties delivers the highest yield among the trio at 7.30%, along with an 83.18% payout ratio. As an experiential REIT focused on gaming, hospitality, and entertainment properties, VICI owns the buildings and land behind casinos, resorts, and entertainment venues. It leases them to operators on long-term contracts. Those leases typically include rent increases tied to inflation.

The company offers a quarterly dividend of $0.46 per share. In its recent Q3 earnings report, VICI reported AFFO of $0.62 per share for the quarter. So VICI paid out roughly 74% of its AFFO per share in the third quarter ($0.46 dividend vs. $0.62 AFFO). Its Q3 2026 earnings per share (EPS) was $0.31.

2. Realty Income (Yield: 5.50% | Payout Ratio: 224.09%)

Realty Income offers a 5.50% yield, with a 224.09% payout ratio based on earnings. As a net lease REIT, Realty Income owns commercial properties leased to retail and other tenants on long-term contracts. The company has a presence across 50 U.S. states, the United Kingdom, and eight other European countries. It is a dividend aristocrat, having raised its dividend for more than 32 consecutive years.

The company pays a monthly dividend of $0.2715 per share, or about $0.81 a quarter. In its Q3 earnings report last week, Realty Income reported AFFO of $1.12 per share. That means Realty Income paid out roughly 73% of its AFFO per share in the third quarter ($0.81 dividend vs. $1.12 AFFO). Its Q3 2026 EPS was $0.43.

3. Agree Realty (Yield: 4.56% | Payout Ratio: 164.16%)

Agree Realty offers a lower yield of 4.56%, with a 164.16% payout ratio. Agree owns retail net-lease properties leased long-term to investment-grade tenants such as Walmart (WMT) and Costco (COST). As of September 30, 2026, the company owns and operates a portfolio of 2,888 properties across the U.S.

The company pays a monthly dividend of $0.27 per share, which is about $0.81 quarterly. According to its Q3 earnings report released last month, Agree has an average AFFO payout ratio of about 74% over the past 10 years. Agree’s AFFO was $1.15 per share for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, and the company paid out roughly 69% of that AFFO. Its Q3 2026 EPS was $0.53.

Conclusion

All three REITs cover their dividends with some cushion, based on their AFFO, though they offer different mixes of yield and stability. VICI offers a higher yield, Realty Income has a dividend track record, and Agree Realty has a lower payout ratio.

data.title: PayPal’s (PYPL) Turnaround Still Needs Proof
data.description:
PayPal’s (PYPL) turnaround still needs more proof, even after its Q3 FY2026 report showed higher adjusted earnings per share (EPS) and an improved full-year outlook. PayPal Holdings operates a global digital-payments network spanning its PayPal and Venmo wallets, branded checkout, Braintree payment processing, credit products, and other merchant services. At the end of 2025, its network connected 440 million active accounts across roughly 200 markets.

There is progress. PayPal’s Q3 FY2026 revenue increased 2% year-over-year to $8.58 billion; transaction margin dollars rose 2% to $4 billion.  Non-GAAP EPS climbed 8% to $1.45, and total payment volume (TPV) also advanced 6% to $487.1 billion.

Still, revenue fell short of Wall Street’s roughly $8.71 billion estimate, while the company’s most important branded checkout business remained sluggish. That tension keeps me neutral on PYPL with a Hold rating. 

PayPal’s EPS Growth Doesn’t Tell the Whole Story

PayPal’s EPS growth doesn’t tell the whole story, especially when you look at its underlying profitability. Non-GAAP EPS rose 8% to $1.45, above the $1.31 consensus estimate, and management raised its full-year adjusted EPS forecast to about $5.60 from roughly $5.38 previously, which is encouraging.

Yet looking above EPS makes the picture less convincing. Non-GAAP net income declined 3% year-over-year to $1.25 billion, while GAAP net income fell 14% to $1.07 billion. PayPal’s share count has also fallen sharply: shares outstanding were down 8.8% year-over-year as of early November. In other words, repurchases are helping per-share earnings grow faster than the underlying profit pool.

This does not make the EPS growth meaningless. Buybacks create value when shares are repurchased cheaply. Yet a lasting rerating probably requires revenue and transaction margins to accelerate as well. Freedom Capital Markets analyst Mikhail Paramonov made a similar point when he downgraded PYPL to Hold in early November, arguing that recent EPS growth reflected expense discipline and a lower share count rather than a clear acceleration in the core business.

Branded Checkout Remains the Missing Piece

Branded checkout remains the missing piece in PayPal’s turnaround, and it’s the main reason I’m reluctant to become bullish. Online branded checkout payment volume growth has remained around 1%–2% for four consecutive quarters, and management expects a similar pace through the fourth quarter.

Branded checkout has historically been one of PayPal’s more valuable businesses. The company itself acknowledges intense competition across digital wallets and payment methods, with consumers and merchants able to choose among bank products, card networks and competing payment technologies.

There are brighter spots. Braintree Total Payment Volume (TPV) grew about 10% in Q3 FY2026, while Venmo produced mid-teens volume growth. Management also expects financial services to contribute more than 20% of transaction margin dollars in 2026, with double-digit growth.

These businesses do not eliminate the need to stabilize PayPal-branded checkout. Until product updates begin taking share or meaningfully accelerating growth, I think investors should keep questioning whether the broader transformation is changing PayPal’s competitive position or merely improving efficiency around a slow-growing core.

PayPal’s Cash Flow and Buybacks Provide Support

PayPal’s cash flow and buybacks provide some reassurance, making a bearish rating difficult to justify. The company generated $1.43 billion in free cash flow (FCF) and $2.05 billion in adjusted FCF in Q3 FY2026. Management now expects at least $6.5 billion in adjusted FCF for the Fiscal year 2026.

PayPal also repurchased roughly $1.5 billion of stock during the quarter and $6 billion over the trailing 12 months and continued returning capital to shareholders, with its board declaring a quarterly dividend of $0.14 per share.

The caveat here is that Q3 FY 2026 FCF fell 17% year-over-year from $1.72 billion. Even so, PayPal’s ability to generate several billion dollars of annual cash flow gives management considerable room to reduce the share count and invest in the turnaround. This is what keeps PayPal out of Sell territory for me.

PayPal’s Valuation

At its current price, PayPal trades at roughly 10.6x forward price-to-earnings (P/E) and 11x trailing earnings. This is a substantial compression from earlier years. PayPal traded at roughly 18.2x forward P/E at the end of FY 2024, and its five-year average forward P/E is 16x. The current multiple is also far below Visa’s (V) forward P/E of about 28.1x and Mastercard’s (MA) 32.7x.

The discount makes PYPL look inexpensive, but I would not call it obviously mispriced. Visa and Mastercard have different business models and stronger recent growth profiles, while PayPal still needs to demonstrate that branded checkout can reaccelerate. The low multiple already reflects this, which supports a Hold rather than either extreme.

What Could Change My Hold Thesis?

A sustained rebound in branded checkout could change my Hold thesis and push me toward a Buy rating, particularly if PayPal pairs it with stronger transaction-margin growth. Faster monetization of Venmo and financial services would strengthen that case. Management’s plan to deliver at least $1.5 billion of gross run-rate cost savings over the next two to three years could provide another lever if those savings translate into durable earnings rather than being fully reinvested.

The downside case is equally clear. Continued market-share pressure in checkout, weaker consumer spending, or further deterioration in FCF would make the low valuation look less like an opportunity and more like a value trap. 

Wall Street’s Outlook for PYPL

Wall Street remains cautious on PYPL, with a Hold consensus rating based on three Buys, 22 Holds, and four Sells over the past three months. At $57.60, the average analyst price target implies about 2.77% downside from the last price of $59.24.

Recent analyst revisions reflect similar hesitation about PayPal’s turnaround. Freedom Capital analyst Mikhail Paramonov downgraded the stock from Buy to Hold and cut his price target from $72 to $63 as the company’s core business continues to struggle to stabilize. TD Cowen analyst Bryan Bergin raised his target from $59 to $60 but kept a Hold rating, noting progress in Venmo and PayPal’s financial services business.

Conclusion

Both analysts see room for improvement, but neither sees enough evidence to justify a Buy rating, and I share their caution. PayPal’s attractive valuation and cash generation offer some reassurance, but until branded checkout improves meaningfully, I believe a Hold remains the more reasonable stance.

data.title: These 2 Dividend Stocks Yield Up to 12% — Bank of America Sees a Buying Opportunity
data.description:
Last week was a wild ride for Wall Street, as investors struggled to make sense of a political shake-up that could have serious consequences for the stock market.

The Democrats’ decisive win in the midterm elections, which handed them control of both the House and Senate, raised concerns about tighter regulations, particularly for tech companies investing heavily in AI and data centers. With fears of higher operating costs and restrictions on future construction adding to existing worries about stretched valuations, investors wasted little time cutting their exposure to riskier assets. By Friday’s closing bell, the S&P 500 had lost 2.7% for the week, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq suffered a 3.4% drop.

When market turbulence starts making investors nervous, many begin looking for ways to make their portfolios more defensive. One popular approach is turning to dividend-paying stocks, which can provide a steady stream of income even when share prices are heading in the wrong direction.

Of course, dividends offer no guarantee against losses, and companies can reduce their payouts if financial conditions deteriorate. This is why investors should look for stocks that combine attractive dividend yields with solid financial fundamentals.

Enter Bank of America analyst Derek Hewett, who has pinpointed two dividend stocks he believes are worth buying at current prices. Both have struggled since the beginning of the year, but they now offer dividend yields of up to 12%. Despite their disappointing stock performance, Hewett sees reasons to remain confident in their financial strength and longer-term prospects, along with the potential for a rebound in their share prices.

In fact, Hewett has plenty of company on Wall Street; both dividend stocks carry Strong Buy consensus ratings, according to the TipRanks database. Let’s see what makes these two names worth considering.

Barings BDC (BBDC)

Bank of America’s first pick, Barings BDC, operates in a corner of the financial market that many everyday investors rarely encounter. Rather than lending money to consumers or large corporations, the company provides financing to middle-market businesses, primarily through privately negotiated loans. These investments generate interest income, much of which eventually makes its way into shareholders’ pockets through quarterly dividend payments.

What makes Barings BDC particularly appealing is the combination of its income-generating portfolio and the financial backing of Barings, a global investment manager specializing in private credit. The company also benefits from credit support arrangements with its external manager, Barings, which provide protection against certain investment losses under specified conditions, although their coverage is limited.

And judging by its latest earnings report, released last Thursday, the company’s financial position remains relatively steady. Third-quarter investment income totaled $64.3 million, while net investment income reached $27.2 million, or $0.26 per share, matching Wall Street’s expectations. Meanwhile, net assets resulting from operations increased by $24.6 million, equivalent to $0.24 per share.

Then there’s the dividend, arguably the biggest reason income investors might want to take a closer look. With a quarterly distribution of $0.26 per share, Barings BDC offers an annualized payout of $1.04, translating into a forward dividend yield of about 12%.

So why has the stock lost about 6% since the beginning of the year? Part of the answer lies in concerns about credit quality and the possibility that lower interest rates could squeeze future investment income. An increase in nonaccrual loans, where borrowers are no longer generating recognized interest income, has added to those worries.

Yet, while these concerns have weighed on investor sentiment, Bank of America’s Derek Hewett sees a more encouraging picture emerging from the company’s latest quarterly results, suggesting the market may be overlooking some of its underlying strengths.

“Barings BDC reported a relatively good quarter as core EPS was in line with Consensus, NAV/share was stable, and the portfolio was modestly higher. While nonaccruals increased, overall levels remain well below peer levels, and the CSA adds another layer of protection for shareholders. Despite the more complex operating backdrop, we think BBDC is well positioned to generate attractive risk-adjusted returns,” Hewett opined.

Based on that confidence, Hewett assigns BBDC shares a Buy rating and a $10 price target, pointing to about 16% upside from current levels. (To watch Hewett’s track record, click here)

And the broader analyst community appears to share much of that confidence. Three of the four analysts covering BBDC recommend buying the stock, while the remaining expert prefers to sit on the fence. Together, those recommendations give the high-yield dividend stock a Strong Buy consensus rating, with an average 12-month price target of $9.63, suggesting another 11.40% in potential share price gains.

Add the stock’s 12% forward dividend yield to the equation, and investors could be looking at a combined potential return of 23.4% over the next year. (See BBDC stock forecast)

Sixth Street Specialty Lending (TSLX)

Next on Bank of America’s list is Sixth Street Specialty Lending, another business development company that has built its reputation around lending to middle-market businesses. But there’s an important difference in how this lender approaches the market. Rather than competing for every available deal, Sixth Street focuses on finding opportunities where it can negotiate favorable terms while keeping a close eye on the possibility that borrowers might run into financial trouble.

The company primarily invests in senior secured loans, which generally give lenders priority over other creditors if a borrower defaults. It also draws on the resources of its parent organization, Sixth Street, a global investment firm overseeing more than $140 billion in assets and committed capital. That combination of lending expertise and access to privately negotiated transactions helps explain why Bank of America considers TSLX particularly well-positioned among its peers.

And its latest quarterly results, released last Tuesday, provided some evidence that the strategy is holding up. Sixth Street reported third-quarter adjusted net investment income of $0.44 per share, matching Wall Street’s expectations. Total investment income reached $98.96 million, exceeding analysts’ forecasts by $1.06 million.

For dividend investors, the appeal is easy to understand. Sixth Street recently declared another quarterly base dividend of $0.42 per share, equivalent to $1.68 annually. At the recent share price of $17.65, that works out to a forward dividend yield of about 9.5%. The company also announced a supplemental distribution of $0.01 per share, providing a little extra income beyond its regular payout.

Still, TSLX shares have lost nearly 19% since the beginning of the year, with much of the damage occurring in February. The selloff reflected growing concerns about private credit, particularly lenders’ exposure to software companies facing potential disruption from AI. Investors worried that weakening borrowers could translate into loan losses, while broader uncertainty surrounding credit quality made BDC stocks less appealing. Lower interest rates and tighter lending spreads have also raised concerns about future investment income.

Bank of America’s Hewett, however, believes Sixth Street’s latest results demonstrate why the company deserves a more favorable assessment than its recent stock performance might suggest.

“Sixth Street reported a solid quarter, with core EPS in line with BofA/Consensus. Positively, net loan growth turned positive, the portfolio yield rose, and non-accruals declined modestly. NAV/share was largely stable. That said, new-deal spreads compressed and the watch list increased. We continue to view TSLX as one of the best positioned BDCs given its late-cycle focus and proprietary origination platform,” Hewett noted.

Hewett backs that confidence with a Buy rating and a $19.50 price target, implying a 10.5% upside from the current share price.

Overall, Wall Street appears largely convinced that Sixth Street has more to offer investors. Five of the six analysts following TSLX recommend buying its shares, with only one maintaining a Hold rating. This translates into a Strong Buy consensus, while the average price target of $18.92 suggests a 7.2% gain over the next 12 months. The picture becomes more appealing when dividends enter the equation, bringing the potential annual return to nearly 16.7%. (See TSLX stock forecast)

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed in this article are solely those of the featured analyst. The content is intended to be used for informational purposes only. It is very important to do your own analysis before making any investment.

On TipRanks, MTDR has a Strong Buy consensus rating based on 12 Buys and four Hold ratings. The average Matador Resources price target of $68.79 implies 36.6% upside potential from current levels.

Diamondback Energy – Diamondback Energy is an oil and natural gas producer focused primarily on the Permian Basin in West Texas. data.title: Pfizer (PFE) Stock Looks Attractive for Income Investors
data.description:
Pfizer (PFE) stock looks attractive for income investors because of its well-covered dividend and modest valuation. The drug maker’s shares have outperformed the S&P 500 (SPX) in 2026, mirroring the strong performance of the healthcare sector as tracked by the iShares U.S. Healthcare ETF (IYH). While broader sector gains are largely driven by growth investors looking to diversify away from the artificial intelligence (AI) theme in stocks such as Eli Lilly (LLY), Pfizer’s investment case is somewhat unique.

No doubt Pfizer reported weaker revenues in Q3 2026, and its adjusted earnings per share (EPS) remain flat relative to the prior-year quarter. However, the shares offer a well-covered dividend of $1.72 per share per year. What is more, they trade at only 10.58x expected 2027 EPS of $2.91.

As such, my Buy rating on Pfizer is driven by a discounted income play in the short term, potentially transforming into a growth investment opportunity if the company’s expectations for a turnaround in sales after 2028 prove correct.

Pfizer’s Q3 2026 Results Highlights

Pfizer reported a marginal 0.4% year-over-year revenue decline to $16.6 billion, impacted by weak demand for COVID-19 treatments and patent expirations. Against this weak top-line result, adjusted EPS of $0.87 was unchanged relative to the prior-year quarter. This was actually a beat as analysts were expecting a weaker earnings print.

Despite unfavorable year-over-year comparisons, results beat the company’s expectations. This prompted Pfizer to raise its full-year revenue guidance to $62–$64 billion, from the previous guidance of $60.5–$62.5 billion. The revised guidance implies a modest 0.6% increase relative to 2025 revenues of $62.6 billion.

For earnings, Pfizer’s 2026 forecast now reflects adjusted EPS of $2.95–$3.05. Using the midpoint, this is still about a 7% decline from the $3.22 EPS achieved in 2025. The silver lining is that weaker profitability reflects higher research and development spending, which should support Pfizer earnings over the medium to long term.

I believe the takeaway for investors is that Pfizer is still struggling to grow revenue and earnings, making the shares primarily appealing to income-focused investors in the short term. Case in point, Pfizer made no share repurchases in 2026, allowing the company to maintain a $0.43 per share quarterly dividend.

Relative to the adjusted EPS forecast for 2026, we see that Pfizer’s annual dividend of $1.72 per share represents a payout of about 57%. I think this makes the dividend quite safe and reinforces my Buy rating on PFE.

Pfizer Targets Growth After 2028

Looking ahead to 2027, we see that analysts expect Pfizer to deliver revenues of about $60 billion, indicating that the top-line pressures observed in Q3 2026 will carry into next year. The same applies to earnings, with consensus EPS estimates standing at about $2.91, pointing to a single-digit decline next year.

Pfizer is keen to highlight that while patent expirations will weigh on near-term growth, the outlook after 2028 remains bright. Growth in Launched and Acquired Products, a category that includes recently launched and acquired products, including new indications, grew 32% year-over-year. As such, the company is able to successfully launch new medicines, supporting a Buy rating on the shares for investors with a medium-to-long-term outlook.

I believe that once the effects of patent expirations are in the rearview mirror, Pfizer’s valuation should move closer to that of large-cap U.S. peers, as I will discuss in the next section.

Pfizer Valuation

Pfizer trades at 10.58x expected 2027 EPS of about $2.91, notably cheaper than peers such as Eli Lilly and Johnson & Johnson (JNJ). For example, Eli Lilly trades at a 28.27x multiple to its expected 2027 EPS of $50.15, while Johnson & Johnson trades at 23.78x its expected 2027 EPS of $11.62.

The key difference between Pfizer and these two peers is that Pfizer’s earnings are still falling, while Eli Lilly is projected to grow earnings by about 42% next year, with a somewhat smaller increase of about 4% penciled in for Johnson & Johnson.

I believe that the key catalyst for Pfizer shares to re-rate higher will be a turnaround in the company’s earnings momentum. While the timing of such a turnaround is hard to pinpoint in advance, I think it may come as early as 2029. My positive outlook is largely driven by the company’s own expectations for a turnaround in sales, although I should caution that higher revenues may not automatically translate into higher earnings per share.

In a nutshell, my Buy rating on Pfizer is driven by a well-covered dividend in the short term and the prospect of higher earnings in the medium-to-long term. Indeed, with an increased focus on longevity and well-being, healthcare stocks will likely continue to do well, although I do admit that the sector is not as cheap following its strong performance in 2026.

Wall Street’s Take on Pfizer

On Wall Street, Pfizer has a Moderate Buy consensus rating, based on seven Buy, 14 Hold, and one Sell ratings over the past three months. The average Pfizer price target is currently $30.26, implying roughly 2% downside over the next 12 months.

Conclusion

Pfizer shares have done well in 2026 even as the company is struggling to achieve meaningful revenue and earnings growth. As such, I believe the broader healthcare sector’s strong performance has boosted Pfizer stock.

In the near term, I see no quick turnaround for Pfizer’s operating performance, as patent expirations continue to weigh on sales and earnings. Against this backdrop, Pfizer’s well-covered dividend remains a key appeal for the investment case.

Over the medium to long term, I expect Pfizer to return to top-line growth. This in turn should support an acceleration in earnings, allowing Pfizer shares to re-rate to a higher earnings multiple, akin to large peers such as Eli Lilly and Johnson & Johnson.

While the stock offers limited capital-gain potential, I think its income appeal remains quite strong, ultimately resulting in an acceptable total return in the near term until revenues return to growth after 2028.

data.title: 3 Best Vanguard Dividend ETFs That Could Power Your Early Retirement
data.description:
Vanguard offers several dividend ETFs that can help investors earn regular income while building long-term wealth. For those planning to retire early, these funds provide exposure to dividend-paying companies and can add stable income to a retirement portfolio. Using TipRanks’ Best Vanguard ETFs tool, three income-focused options stand out: Vanguard High Dividend Yield Index ETF (VYM), Vanguard International Dividend Appreciation ETF (VIGI), and Vanguard Energy ETF (VDE).

These ETFs offer stable dividend yields, along with income and potential for long-term growth. This can help investors build wealth over time and work toward early retirement. According to TipRanks’ unique ETF analyst consensus, determined based on a weighted average of analyst ratings on its holdings, VDE, VYM, and VIGI are rated Moderate Buys. Based on average price targets, VYM offers 15% upside, followed by VIGI at 14% and VDE at 8%.

Vanguard High Dividend Yield Index ETF (VYM)

The Vanguard High Dividend Yield ETF is a key part of Vanguard’s dividend lineup. It follows a straightforward approach by investing in a wide range of stocks that pay higher-than-average dividends.

VYM pays a quarterly dividend of $0.89 per share, reflecting a 2.24% yield. Its market-cap weighting gives larger companies more influence in the fund. This approach may also reduce exposure to smaller companies offering unusually high dividend yields.

VYM holds 594 stocks and has $83.87 billion in assets. Its top three holdings are Broadcom (AVGO), JPMorgan (JPM), and Exxon Mobil Corp. (XOM).

Vanguard Energy ETF (VDE)

The Vanguard Energy ETF (VDE) offers investors low-cost, broad exposure to the U.S. energy sector. Because many energy companies generate strong cash flow and return a portion of it to shareholders, VDE has historically offered a higher dividend yield than the broader market.

VDE has a dividend yield of 2.09% and pays a $1.05 quarterly dividend.

In terms of holdings, VDE holds stocks involved in oil and gas exploration, production, refining, equipment services, and midstream infrastructure. Its top 3 holdings are XOM, Chevron (CVX), and ConocoPhillips (COP). Overall, VDE holds 113 stocks with total assets worth $11.63 billion.

Vanguard International Dividend Appreciation ETF (VIGI)

The Vanguard International Dividend Appreciation ETF (VIGI) gives investors exposure to a wide range of international companies with a focus on dividend growth. The ETF tracks the Nasdaq International Dividend Achievers Select Index, which includes companies outside the U.S. that have consistently increased their dividend payments over time.

VIGI has a dividend yield of 2.13% and pays a $0.46 quarterly dividend.  In terms of holdings, VIGI owns 338 stocks with assets worth $9.19 billion.

data.title: Chevron Stock (CVX) Still Looks Attractive Even if Oil Prices Fall
data.description:
Chevron (CVX) stock still looks attractive, even if oil prices fall, in my view. The integrated energy producer posted $10.4 billion in adjusted Q3 earnings. Wall Street expects profits to decline over the next two years. However, I remain bullish because Chevron can keep improving the business as commodity prices normalize.

CEO Mike Wirth said it best: “We’re reinvesting to bring more energy to a supply-constrained market.” That investment should play a critical role in Chevron’s investment case beyond today’s exceptional prices. Chevron is building a larger production base while lowering costs.

Chevron’s Q3 Delivered Exceptional Cash Flow

Chevron’s Q3 delivered exceptional cash flow, giving shareholders plenty to like. October 30 results showed adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of $5.28, beating expectations near $4.87.

Production reached 3.98 million barrels of oil equivalent daily. U.S. upstream output was 27% above two years earlier, helped by Hess (HESM). Adjusted free cash flow reached $14.2 billion, although asset sales and a Tengiz loan repayment contributed. Standard free cash flow was still $12 billion. Chevron distributed $6 billion to shareholders and reduced debt by $3.5 billion.

Higher oil prices helped compared with last year, but refining deserves particular attention. Downstream earnings reached $4.93 billion. U.S. refineries ran at 98% utilization, processing a record 1.09 million barrels daily.

The key is the gap between crude costs and finished-fuel prices. Disrupted diesel supplies can widen that gap. Running its refineries reliably allowed Chevron to process more barrels while those economics were favorable.

Those conditions could persist near term. Brent (CM:BZ) fell 4.2% to $108.66 on November 2 as talks raised hopes of ending the U.S.-Iran war. Yet Abu Dhabi National Oil Company’s (ADNOC) CEO says nearly one billion barrels have left global inventories since Hormuz shipping was disrupted. Some regions’ seasonal diesel inventories are at 35-year lows. Rebuilding those buffers could support demand even after shipping improves.

That said, I don’t think it makes sense to assume another quarter matches Q3. In fact, Q4 downtime could remove 175,000–225,000 boe/day. Downstream maintenance could also cost $400 million–$500 million in earnings. A lasting geopolitical settlement could quickly reduce oil prices and refining margins.

Lower Costs Can Sustain Earnings

In any case, Chevron’s lower costs can sustain earnings as the commodity cycle cools. Hess brought a 30% interest in Guyana’s Stabroek Block. Its more than 11 billion boe of discovered recoverable resources support development into the 2030s. Chevron has already achieved $1.5 billion of annual Hess synergies, exceeding the original target six months early.

The expanded Tengiz operation also provides additional production without repeating the initial construction bill. Meanwhile, Chevron is sustaining Permian output above one million boe/day with greater capital efficiency. Gulf project ramp-ups also contribute. Management’s broader plan targets 2%–3% annual upstream production growth through 2030.

Then, note that the October Bakken restructuring should halve unit midstream costs and remove $3.7 billion of consolidated debt. Chevron expects a half-percentage-point improvement in corporate return on capital employed. The trade-off here is surrendering midstream ownership and recognizing a $3 billion–$4 billion accounting loss at closing.

I also believe that Venezuela offers further potential, but, of course, subject to substantial political risk. September agreements support more than $7 billion of joint-venture investment. The ventures aim to more than double gross output to roughly 600,000 barrels daily within five years. That figure includes partners’ production, so it isn’t all Chevron’s.

Chevron’s plan targets over 10% annual adjusted free-cash-flow growth through 2030 at $70 Brent. The company’s capex-and-dividend breakeven should stay below $50 Brent. These are just targets, but they explain my confidence beyond today’s prices. More low-cost production can cushion weaker realizations.

Falling Earnings Still Leave a Reasonable Valuation

After the stock’s tremendous rally, investors now worry about falling earnings if oil prices weaken. However, I believe even that scenario still leaves Chevron at a reasonable valuation. The $18.5 consensus EPS estimate for 2026 implies a 12.31x earnings valuation. Consensus then assumes $16.24 in 2027 and $13.34 in 2028.

Those estimates imply declines of about 12% and 18%, lifting forward multiples to 14.03x and 17.07x. That rising P/E deserves attention, as investors buying today already face a forecast 29% earnings decline by 2028. The shares are near their highs, so it seems like this setup offers limited protection against further disappointments. Still, I find the valuation reasonable for Chevron’s improving portfolio.

Consensus already allows for substantial earnings normalization. If prices hold up better, production gains and lower costs could leave those estimates too low.

Meanwhile, the $1.78 quarterly dividend provides a 3% annualized yield. Chevron has raised dividends for 39 consecutive years. Even against 2028’s $13.16 EPS, today’s $7.12 annual dividend consumes roughly 54% of earnings. Cash coverage is noteworthy, but that payout leaves room for earnings to fall. Management also maintains a $2.5 billion-$3 billion quarterly buyback pace.

At today’s stock price, that budget could retire roughly 2%–3% of shares annually. This can help support EPS as commodity prices weaken. I would assume consensus already includes some repurchases, so buybacks should support the forecasts without being counted as extra upside on top. Also, net debt was just 0.4x trailing operating cash flow, supporting continued investment through weaker markets.

Is Chevron Stock a Buy?

Chevron stock has a Strong Buy consensus, based on 13 Buys and three Holds. The average price target of $248.25 implies 8.99% upside from today’s share price level.

Conclusion

I remain bullish on Chevron because the company can keep strengthening its earnings base as oil normalizes. Today’s exceptional margins provide extra cash, while Guyana and cost reductions support future returns. What we saw in Q3 doesn’t need to become permanent for the investment case to work from here.

data.title: Pfizer (PFE) vs. AstraZeneca (AZN): Which Pharma Stock Offers a Better Dividend?
data.description:
Pfizer (PFE) and AstraZeneca (AZN) are two pharmaceutical companies that offer dividends. Both offer dividend yields above the broader market, but Pfizer offers quarterly dividends, while AstraZeneca pays semiannual dividends.

The TipRanks Stock Comparison tool helps investors compare these dividend stocks across key metrics, including dividend yield, payout ratio, valuation, analyst ratings, and upside.

Pfizer (PFE) — Pfizer is a global pharmaceutical company with a broad portfolio across vaccines, oncology, internal medicine, and prescription medicines. The company is also advancing a pipeline of new treatments and indications as it works to offset the impact of upcoming patent expirations. Pfizer reported Q3 2026 earnings today and posted revenue of $16.6 billion. It raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $62 billion–$64 billion.

The pharma giant offers a dividend yield of 5.61%, above the healthcare sector average of 1.423%. Its payout ratio is 227.81%. Pfizer has been paying a quarterly dividend of $0.43 since Q1 2025. The Q4 2026 cash dividend due in December will be Pfizer’s 352nd consecutive quarterly dividend.

Pfizer has a Moderate Buy consensus on TipRanks, with a $29.62 average PFE stock price target suggesting 3.43% downside from current price levels.

AstraZeneca (AZN) — AstraZeneca is a global biopharmaceutical company focused on oncology, cardiovascular, renal, respiratory, and immunology treatments. According to recent Phase 3 data, Tagrisso, AstraZeneca’s leading EGFR-mutated lung cancer therapy, in combination with Orpathys helped patients with a specific genetic form of lung cancer live significantly longer without their disease worsening. The company reported Q3 2026 earnings on October 30, with quarterly revenue of $16.16 billion. AstraZeneca expects full-year total revenue to grow by a mid-to-high single-digit percentage at constant exchange rates (CER).

The biopharma developer offers a dividend yield of 1.73%, above the healthcare sector average of 1.423%. AstraZeneca pays dividends twice a year, with a larger second interim payment later in the year. Its payout ratio is 45.40%.

AstraZeneca has a Strong Buy consensus rating, with 14 of the 16 Wall Street analysts covering the stock rating it a Buy. The average AZN stock price target of $215.90 implies 15.72% upside from the last price.

Conclusion

Pfizer offers the higher dividend yield, making it more appealing to income-focused investors, though its high payout ratio raises questions about long-term coverage. AstraZeneca offers a lower yield but a more conservative payout ratio and stronger growth expectations, which may appeal to investors prioritizing dividend sustainability and total return.

data.title: Western Digital (WDC) Raises Dividend 16.7% Following Strong Earnings
data.description:
Data storage company Western Digital Corp. (WDC) has raised its quarterly dividend by 16.7% days after reporting strong quarterly financial results. The company has declared a quarterly distribution of $0.175 per share, up 16.7% from its previous dividend of $0.15. The new dividend is payable on Dec. 17 of this year to shareholders of record as of Dec. 4.

The increased dividend gives WDC stock a forward yield of 0.20%. This is the second consecutive year that Western Digital has increased its dividend as its financial results are powered higher by demand for its data storage products in artificial intelligence (AI) data centers. Growing demand from AI led the company to recently report financial results that exceeded Wall Street’s expectations.

Western Digital’s key performance indicators. Source: TipRanks

Western Digital’s Latest Print

The company, a maker of data storage systems and hard disk drives, reported earnings per share (EPS) of $4.64, beating the $4.08 consensus estimate among analysts. Revenue in what was the company’s fiscal 2027 first quarter totaled $4.38 billion, up 55% year-over-year and topping the $4.14 billion that was expected on Wall Street.

Western Digital’s gross margin came in at 58.1%, up from 43.9% a year ago. The company’s operating margin was 49.1%. Western Digital’s data storage products and disk drives are widely used in AI data centers. WDC stock has nearly tripled (up more than 190%) in the last 12 months.

Western Digital’s Outlook

In terms of guidance, Western Digital said that it expects revenue in the current quarter of $5 billion to $5.2 billion. The midpoint of that range, $5.1 billion, is above the $4.57 billion consensus forecast among analysts. Management at Western Digital said that the company’s operating cash flow in the latest quarter totaled $1.60 billion, while its free cash flow reached $1.38 billion.

The company also said that it expects earnings of $5.60 to $6.00 per share. The midpoint of that range, $5.80, is well above the $4.82 expected on Wall Street. In the company’s earnings statement, Western Digital CEO Irving Tan said: “We are executing well through our technology transitions to meet the growing demand for storage.”

Is WDC Stock a Buy?

Western Digital’s stock has a consensus Strong Buy rating among 17 Wall Street analysts. That rating is based on 14 Buy and three Hold recommendations issued in the last three months. The average WDC price target of $649.56 implies 84% upside from current levels.

data.title: Interactive Brokers Stock (IBKR) Struggles Despite Strong Financial Results and Huge Dividend Increase
data.description:
The stock of Interactive Brokers (IBKR) continues to struggle despite the online trading platform recently reporting strong financial results and a massive 71% increase to its quarterly dividend payment. IBKR stock is now down 7% over the past month despite the positive news of its earnings and increased distribution to shareholders.

The current decline comes after a greater than 20% rise in the share price over the past 12 months. In the last five years, IBKR stock has gained 360% as the fast-growing brokerage impressed Wall Street with its financial results and new customer accounts. It appears that the stock got a head of expectations and that the share price is now experiencing a reset. IBKR stock trades at a rich valuation of 31 times future earnings estimates.

Interactive Brokers’ dividends per share. Source: TipRanks

IBKR’s Financial Results

Interactive Brokers reported third-quarter earnings per share (EPS) of $0.69, which topped the $0.67 consensus estimate among analysts. The firm’s revenue for the July through September quarter totaled $1.91 billion, which was ahead of the $1.86 billion forecast on Wall Street. Like other brokerages, Interactive Brokers has benefited this year from strong trading activity among investors as the stock market rose to successive all-time highs.

Customer accounts at the firm increased 35% year-over-year in the third quarter to 5.58 million. Total daily average trades on its platform increased 18% to 4.27 million. Additionally, margin loans at Interactive Brokers increased 36% to $105.2 billion. When customers use margin, they are borrowing money from their brokerage to buy stocks.

However, despite the strong headline numbers, there are signs of a slowdown at Interactive Brokers. Customer trading in stocks was down 24% year-over-year in the third quarter while trading in options contracts decreased 1%. That news helped send IBKR stock lower in recent days.

The Big Dividend Increase

A few days after its latest print, Interactive Brokers raised its quarterly dividend by 71%. The stock trading platform lifted its distribution to shareholders to $0.15 per share each quarter from $0.0875 previously. The new dividend takes the yield on IBKR stock close to 1% from 0.41% previously.

The new dividend is scheduled to be paid on Dec. 14 of this year to shareholders of record as of Dec. 1. This is the second consecutive year that the company has raised its distribution. Interactive Brokers had maintained a modest quarterly dividend payout of $0.025 for several years. But since the end of 2024, the company has raised its quarterly dividend by 500%.

Is IBKR Stock a Buy?

Interactive Brokers’ stock has a consensus Strong Buy rating among 12 Wall Street analysts. That rating is based on nine Buy and three Hold recommendations issued in the last three months. The average IBKR price target of $106.64 implies 25% upside from current levels. These ratings could change after the company’s financial results.

data.title: Visa (V) Reports Strong Financial Results and Raises Dividend by 16%
data.description:
Credit card giant Visa (V) has reported quarterly financial results that beat Wall Street forecasts and raised its quarterly dividend by 16%. The San Francisco-based company announced earnings per share (EPS) of $3.48, which beat the consensus estimate among analysts of $3.44. Revenue in the period totaled $12.1 billion, matching consensus estimates. Sale were up 13% from a year earlier.

The latest results were for the fourth quarter of Visa’s 2026 fiscal year. As such, they also included numbers for the entire year. Visa posted fiscal 2026 full-year revenue of $45.9 billion, up 15% year-over-year. Full-year earnings per share came in at $13.27, representing 16% annual growth for the company. The full-year figures were largely in line with Visa’s own guidance.

Visa’s key performance indicators. Source: TipRanks

Visa’s Credit Card Transactions

Management at Visa said that the company’s credit card network handled 74.2 billion transactions during the latest quarter, an increase of 10% from the same period of 2025. Cross-border transaction volumes rose 14% globally, reflecting robust international travel and spending using Visa’s cards. Total payment volumes grew 9% on a constant-dollar basis.

In terms of guidance, Visa said that it expects earnings growth for all of fiscal 2027 in the low double digits to low teens. That represents a slowdown from 16% growth in the just completed 2026 fiscal year. Revenue for in the year ahead is expected in the low double digits versus 15% in fiscal 2026. For the current quarter, Visa expects earnings and revenue growth to each be in the low double digits.

Visa’s Dividend

Along with its financial results, Visa raised its quarterly dividend 16% to $0.78 a share from $0.67 previously. The new dividend will give V stock a yield of about 0.75%. Visa has raised its dividend every year since its 2008 initial public offering (IPO). Visa has increased its distribution to stockholders by more than 550% since going public.

Is V Stock a Buy?

The stock of Visa has a consensus Strong Buy rating among 28 Wall Street analysts. That rating is based on 26 Buy and two Hold recommendations issued in the last three months. The average V price target of $425.54 implies 10% upside from current levels. These ratings could change after the company’s financial results.

data.title: AT&T (T) vs. Verizon (VZ): Which Telecom Stock Offers a Better Dividend?
data.description:
AT&T (T) and Verizon (VZ) are two U.S. telecom companies that offer quarterly dividends. Both offer dividend yields well above the broader market. Investors typically consider three things when comparing these dividend stocks: yield, payment track record, and how comfortably earnings and cash flow cover the payout.

The TipRanks Stock Comparison tool helps investors compare these dividend stocks based on their dividend yield, payout ratio, date of payout, dividend amount, and more.

AT&T (T) — AT&T provides mobile phone service, 5G wireless connectivity, and high-speed fiber Internet to consumers and businesses. It builds and operates the wireless and fiber-optic networks that carry voice and data traffic. In its Q3 2026 earnings released last week, free cash flow was $5 billion. The company guided free cash flow to at least $18 billion for 2026, more than $19 billion for 2027, and over $21 billion for 2028. It has a market cap of $141.06 billion.

AT&T offers a dividend yield of 5.3%, above the communications sector average of 1.209%. Its payout ratio is 59.85%. The company has been paying dividends for over 40 years. Since 2022, AT&T has paid a quarterly dividend of $0.2775 per share, or $1.11 annually.

Verizon (VZ) — Verizon provides wireless service, including 5G, and home Internet through its Fios fiber network, fixed wireless access, and the Frontier fiber business it acquired to consumers and businesses. It is one of the world’s largest telecom companies by revenue. Verizon published its third-quarter results earlier this week. Free cash flow for the first nine months of 2026 was $18 billion.

In Q3, free cash flow was $7.8 billion, up 12.1% year-over-year. Verizon expects free cash flow growth to approach 12% in 2026 over the prior year. Its market cap is about $182.52 billion. The company has raised its dividend for 20 consecutive years. Verizon offers a dividend yield of 6.4%, higher than the communications sector yield of 1.209%. Its dividend payout ratio is 71.75%.

Conclusion

Verizon offers the higher dividend yield and a longer record of dividend increases. Verizon may appeal to those prioritizing current income and a history of increases, while AT&T’s lower payout ratio may be relevant to those focused on dividend coverage.

data.title: Jersey Mike’s (JMKE) Announces Special Dividend Along with Financial Results
data.description:
U.S. restaurant chain Jersey Mike’s (JMKE) has announced a special dividend payment to its stockholders alongside its latest financial results. The chain of sandwich restaurants said that it will pay a one-time dividend of $0.35 per share. The ex-dividend date and payment date for the special dividend were not included in the company’s earnings release.

The special dividend payout is part of Jersey Mike’s plan to return up to $200 million to shareholders, including a $100 million stock buyback program. The special dividend and share repurchase appear to be an effort by Jersey Mike’s to convince investors to buy its stock, which has slumped since the company held in initial public offering (IPO) on July 30 of this year.

Jersey Mike’s does not currently pay a regular quarterly dividend to its stockholders.

A technical analysis of JMKE stock. Source: TipRanks

Jersey Mike’s Financial Results

This is the second quarterly financial report from Jersey Mike’s since its IPO was held at the end of July. JMKE stock debuted on the New York Stock Exchange at $21 a share. Since then, the share price has fallen as low as $15. As for its latest financial results, Jersey Mike’s reported earnings per share (EPS) of $0.23, which topped the $0.16 that was expected on Wall Street.

Revenue in the company’s fiscal third quarter totaled $209 million, which narrowly beat the $208.5 million consensus forecast of analysts. The company’s same-store sales grew 3% year-over-year in the period, coming in at the low end of expectations for 3.4% growth. The sandwich chain opened 80 new restaurants during the quarter, up from 54 a year earlier and bringing its store count to 3,456 locations.

Jersey Mike’s Guidance

In terms of guidance, Jersey Mike’s maintained its full-year forecast for earnings growth of at least 20%, along with restaurant growth of 8%. However, the restaurant chain now expects same-store sales growth of 2.5%, which has been lowered from a previous range of 2.5% to 3% growth. JMKE stock is up 6% on Oct. 28 following its latest financial results.

The special dividend payment and stock buyback program appear to be giving Jersey Mike’s stock a much needed boost. Analysts say the stock has struggled along with the entire restaurant sector as investors remain weary of the U.S. economy and a pullback in discretionary spending on the part of American consumers.

Is JMKE Stock a Buy?

Jersey Mike’s stock has a consensus Strong Buy rating among 24 Wall Street analysts. That rating is based on 20 Buy and four Hold recommendations issued in the last three months. The average JMKE price target of $27.64 implies 54% upside from current levels. These ratings could change after the company’s financial results.

data.title: Homebuilder D.R. Horton (DHI) Raises Dividend 11%
data.description:
Leading U.S. homebuilder D.R. Horton (DHI) has raised its quarterly dividend payment to shareholders by 11%. Going forward, the company will pay a distribution of $0.50 per share, an 11.1% increase from its previous dividend of $0.45. The new dividend gives DHI stock a yield of 1.37%.

The new distribution is payable on Nov. 19 of this year to shareholders of record as of Nov. 12. D.R. Horton has now raised its dividend payment for 13 consecutive years. Over the last decade, the company’s dividend has averaged a 19% annual growth rate.

D.R. Horton’s dividend payments. Source: TipRanks

D.R. Horton’s Earnings

Arlington, Texas-based D.R. Horton is the biggest homebuilder by volume in America. The latest dividend increase comes despite the company grappling with a weak housing market as consumers struggle with affordability issues and interest rates on home mortgages that are currently above 7%.

The dividend increase was announced along with D.R. Hortons’ latest financial results. For the year’s third quarter, the company reported earnings per share (EPS) of $2.67, missing Wall Street’s consensus forecast of $3. Revenue came in at $9.4 billion, exceeding the analyst consensus estimate of $9.07 billion.

Management at D.R. Horton said the housing market in the U.S. remains challenging with interest rates elevated and consumers taking a cautious approach to home purchases.

Is DHI Stock a Buy?

D.R. Horton stock has a consensus Hold rating among 13 Wall Street analysts. That rating is based on two Buy, nine Hold, and two Sell recommendations issued in the last three months. The average DHI price target of $148.36 implies 2% upside from current levels. These ratings could change after the company’s financial results.
